cohort: 564 children from the WHEALS birth cohort
finding: Planned cesarean delivery was associated with a higher likelihood of belonging to a trajectory of increasing hs-CRP throughout childhood, which partially mediated the association between planned C-section and higher BMI at age 10, suggesting potential long-term benefits of labor exposure.
mod_finding: Children delivered via planned C-section had 1.15 times higher risk of being in the high hs-CRP trajectory class compared to vaginal deliveries, while no association was found for unplanned C-section deliveries.
